# Parks

> Comparison of mapped parks and green spaces across nine cities.
> Static, source-backed, and free of paid map APIs or Google services.

Canonical URL: https://parks.soli.blue/
Language: German
Geographic scope: Berlin, Vienna, Munich, Stuttgart, Madrid, Barcelona, Paris,
Copenhagen, and Cairo

## What the site provides

- A city comparison plus maps and searchable lists for nine cities
- Population-weighted 10-minute access estimates for all nine cities
- Harmonized green-space share, green space per resident, and tree-cover share
- District filters, plus positively matched amenities where source coverage exists
- Optional browser geolocation or a map-selected origin
- Local straight-line distance and 5/10/15-minute estimates
- Visible data source, map attribution, methodology, and freshness

The rings drawn from a selected map point are straight-line estimates. The
city-level access values are separately computed pedestrian-network estimates.
Missing amenity coverage is not evidence of absence.

Leaderboard inputs are distinct from the native local park layers used for map
exploration. All nine comparison inventories use the same OpenStreetMap classes:
leisure=park, leisure=nature_reserve, natural=wood, and landuse=forest, plus
leisure=garden only with explicit public access and no tagged fee. Geometries
are clipped and dissolved. Core classes count toward mapped green land
regardless of access. For routing, fee-tagged or explicitly restricted geometry
is removed; parks, nature reserves, and public gardens qualify by class, woods
and forests require an explicit public-access tag, and routed components must be
at least 0.5 ha.

## Public static data

- https://parks.soli.blue/data/cities.json — city catalog and comparison totals
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/access.json — harmonized comparison metrics and methodology
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/berlin/ — Berlin geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/vienna/ — Vienna geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/munich/ — Munich geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/stuttgart/ — Stuttgart geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/madrid/ — Madrid geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/barcelona/ — Barcelona geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/paris/ — Paris geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/copenhagen/ — Copenhagen geometry, index, summary, sources
- https://parks.soli.blue/data/cairo/ — Cairo geometry, index, summary, sources

These files are build artifacts, not a stability-guaranteed public API. The
city snapshots keep official identifiers where available and stable
city-prefixed OpenStreetMap identifiers for extracted PBF features.

## Sources and terms

Native map data: Land Berlin, Stadt Wien, Ville de Paris, Københavns Kommune,
and OpenStreetMap extracts.
Comparison green space and walking network: OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
Comparison population: EC JRC GHSL GHS-POP 2020, 100 m modeled grid.
Tree cover: Copernicus Global Land Service CGLS-LC100 2019 fractional tree
cover divided by land area from its matching permanent-water fraction, 100 m
(CC BY 4.0). Its documented global tree-fraction MAE is 8.9 percentage points.
Background maps: basemap.de, basemap.at, and OpenFreeMap.
Project code: MIT.
